signals.claim: Transpacific container rates surged sharply in early June 2025 as importers front-loaded cargo during the temporary U.S.-China tariff pause, while vessel/equipment positioning and port congestion constrained near-term capacity.

evidence.summary: Freightos reported Asia-US West Coast rates up 98% to USD5,488/FEU and East Coast rates up 61% to USD6,410/FEU, driven by frontloading ahead of tariff deadlines plus constrained near-term capacity.

A shipping-stock community discussion immediately after the tariff pause explicitly hypothesized a 90-day inventory/frontloading demand shock. This is used only as expectation/discovery evidence, not as confirmation of freight economics.

contraryEvidence.summary: Reuters reported the tariff-driven container-rate surge but also cited signs that the spike could peak soon as late-June quotes softened and capacity returned.
Freightos expected rates could begin easing by mid-July as demand cooled, congestion eased and capacity returned; the frontload was explicitly temporary.

causalChain: temporary tariff pause + deadline risk -> importers pull shipments forward
frontloaded volume + out-of-position vessels/equipment + congestion -> near-term spot-rate spike
container carriers with material transpacific exposure capture higher revenue per TEU while elevated rates persist
earnings benefit fades when frontloading exhausts and capacity returns
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A large container carrier with material transpacific volume/revenue, demonstrated sensitivity of profit to revenue per TEU, strong balance-sheet/cash generation, and a valuation that does not assume the temporary June spike persists for a full cycle.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Near-term positive for carriers with transpacific exposure, but largely a timing/frontloading transfer rather than durable end-demand creation.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Event-repricing / weeks to a few months.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The freight-rate spike was visible, and shipping forums were already discussing the frontload thesis, so the opportunity requires low valuation and earnings sensitivity rather than narrative novelty.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: How much of the June spot-rate surge reaches the carrier's realized blended revenue before capacity and demand normalize.

candidates.name: 中远海控
candidates.economicExposure: 2025Q1 group transpacific volume rose 16.2% YoY and transpacific route revenue rose 26.3%. The company explicitly attributed a 73.1% YoY increase in attributable profit to higher container-shipping volume and revenue per TEU.
candidates.monetization: A sharp June transpacific spot-rate spike can feed into realized revenue per TEU on spot/renewed business. Q1 already showed revenue-per-TEU sensitivity and strong operating cash generation.
earningsBridge: frontloaded transpacific demand and constrained near-term capacity
higher realized revenue per TEU on transpacific/container routes
container-shipping EBIT and operating cash flow

basisReconciliation.externalIndicator: Freightos transpacific spot-rate indices and near-term congestion/frontloading.
basisReconciliation.companyRealizedBasis: Company Q1 disclosures showed material transpacific volume/revenue and directly linked profit growth to higher shipping volume and revenue per TEU.
basisReconciliation.basisRisk: Spot indices are not the company's blended realized rate; contracts, route mix, bunker cost and timing create a basis. The June spike must not be treated as a full-quarter realized rate.

candidates.balanceSheetCycle: 2024 attributable profit was RMB49.17bn and Q1 2025 attributable profit RMB11.69bn; operating cash flow was strong. Shipping remains highly cyclical, so peak-rate annualization is explicitly forbidden.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Large global network, transpacific scale, fleet capacity and strong balance sheet support capture, but industry capacity can respond quickly and this is not a structural moat expansion.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: Several weeks to roughly two months; the frontload should fade as tariff-deadline cargo is shipped, congestion clears and vessels/equipment return.
normalizationIndicators: Freightos/Drewry transpacific spot rates roll over
horizonBridge.whyHorizonMatches: The causal driver is a temporary deadline-induced shipping rush, not durable multi-year demand.

candidates.priceExpectation: Pending deterministic pre-signal price/market-cap enrichment. Candidate status requires valuation that remains acceptable using normalized/cautious profit rather than annualizing the June rate spike.
contraryEvidence: Reuters and Freightos both warned the surge could peak/normalize quickly.
The market and shipping forums were already aware of the frontload thesis.
High spot rates do not map one-for-one into the company's blended realized revenue per TEU.
thesisBreakers: transpacific spot rates reverse before the company can realize higher blended rates
capacity returns faster than expected and erodes GRIs
frontloaded demand exhausts sharply in late June/July
pre-signal valuation already prices a prolonged high-rate cycle
unansweredQuestions: What market-cap/profit scenario does the June 10 share price imply?
How much of transpacific revenue is spot/short-contract enough to reprice within the expected event horizon?

pointInTimeEvidence.summary: 2025Q1 revenue RMB57.96bn, attributable profit RMB11.69bn, operating cash flow RMB15.06bn; transpacific volume +16.2% and route revenue +26.3%; company said profit growth reflected higher volume and revenue per TEU.
2024 attributable profit RMB49.17bn and total annual cash dividend payout around 50% of attributable profit.

signals.claim: China's rare-earth/magnet export licensing restrictions were causing real overseas automotive supply shortages by early June 2025, including temporary production disruptions.

evidence.summary: Reuters reported automaker/supplier production disruptions and warnings linked to Chinese rare-earth and magnet export-license delays.

contraryEvidence.summary: A major A-share magnet producer disclosed material export sales, including U.S. sales, so an export-license bottleneck can constrain the producer's own monetization rather than simply raising its profit.

causalChain: export licensing delays -> ex-China magnet availability falls
scarcity raises strategic value of magnet supply
but Chinese magnet exporters may themselves be blocked from shipping, so headline scarcity does not imply a clean A-share long
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: An A-share magnet/material producer able to monetize scarcity without being constrained by the same export-license rule—e.g. meaningful domestic demand or already-operating offshore production with secured raw material—and with material earnings sensitivity.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Ambiguous for Chinese exporters: strategic scarcity rises but export friction can directly reduce addressable shipments.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Policy-dependent; potentially months, but license approvals can normalize abruptly.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The disruption became highly visible through automaker shutdowns; company-level channel exposure matters more than theme intensity.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether any A-share producer can capture overseas scarcity rather than being constrained by it.

candidates.name: 金力永磁
candidates.economicExposure: 2025Q1 REPM finished-product sales rose more than 40% YoY; NEV/auto parts contributed about half of revenue. Export sales were 17.76% of revenue and U.S. exports 6.94%, proving direct exposure to the affected geography.
candidates.monetization: Existing capacity utilization exceeded 90%, but the same export controls creating overseas scarcity could restrict shipments. High utilization also limits an immediate volume response.
earningsBridge: license-approved export volume / realized magnet pricing

basisReconciliation.externalIndicator: Overseas auto-supply shortages caused by rare-earth/magnet export licensing.
basisReconciliation.companyRealizedBasis: The company had real magnet production, >40% finished-product sales growth and material U.S./export revenue before the cutoff.
basisReconciliation.basisRisk: The company is directly subject to the same export licensing bottleneck, so overseas scarcity can hurt volume even if pricing power improves.

candidates.balanceSheetCycle: Q1 inventory and receivables were high and operating cash flow remained negative, so a headline price/supply squeeze should not be assumed to convert directly into cash earnings.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Scale, high-performance NdFeB capability and high utilization are real advantages, but the policy channel creates a direct constraint.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: Weeks to months because export-license approvals or diplomatic arrangements can change the physical bottleneck quickly.
normalizationIndicators: overseas automakers report restored magnet supply
company export sales fail to grow despite scarcity
horizonBridge.whyHorizonMatches: The observed shortage is caused by a licensing bottleneck, not a slow-moving permanent capacity shortage.

candidates.priceExpectation: Remain Watch unless the economics show the company can monetize the shortage despite being inside the licensing constraint.
contraryEvidence: The company itself had material export/U.S. sales exposed to licensing.
Capacity utilization already exceeded 90%, limiting rapid incremental volume.
Q1 operating cash flow was negative.
thesisBreakers: license delays reduce exports more than scarcity lifts price
high utilization prevents incremental volume capture
unansweredQuestions: What share of U.S. shipments had valid licenses by the cutoff?
Could domestic demand absorb export-constrained output at comparable margins?

finalDecision.noTradeReason: NO TRADE at prefreeze. The real-world shortage is clear, but the obvious A-share magnet producer is constrained by the same licensing mechanism and cannot yet show a clean incremental earnings bridge.

signals.claim: China's photovoltaic manufacturing chain remained in severe overcapacity in June 2025, with module prices below production cost, industry losses and production cuts despite policy efforts to curb expansion.

evidence.summary: Reuters reported persistent PV oversupply, prices below production cost, widespread losses and output reductions; policy attempts had not yet resolved the imbalance.

causalChain: excess manufacturing capacity -> destructive price competition
prices below cost -> losses and production cuts
industry consolidation may eventually improve economics
but before credible capacity exit and price stabilization, a long requires guessing the cycle bottom
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A low-cost PV producer with balance-sheet durability and proof that industry capacity is actually exiting and realized margins are stabilizing—not merely a company that survives longer than peers.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Still contracting at the cutoff; no clean evidence that the industry profit pool had turned.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: Low valuations alone are insufficient while earnings remain below sustainable economics.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: When capacity exit becomes large enough to restore pricing discipline.

finalDecision.noTradeReason: NO TRADE. The signal is a warning about unresolved overcapacity rather than a validated reversal. Do not bottom-fish solely because the sector is distressed.
